notes: §1985:IX.4.6.4 GR5 makes REWRITE ... FROM "equivalent to the execution of the following statements in the order specified": "MOVE identifier-1 TO record-name-1" under the MOVE statement's rules, then "The same REWRITE statement without the FROM phrase." KeyedIoBinder.BindRewrite binds the phrase through MoveBinder.BindFromPhrase, which hands identifier-1 and record-name-1 (the record named, not the widest record of the area) to BindMoveOf, the one application of the MOVE rules; KeyedIoEmitter.EmitRewrite emits that bound move first and then the code path a REWRITE without FROM takes. No edition arm in the move; the one 1985 difference is the gate VersionConformancePass.VisitRecordFromPhrase, which refuses FROM literal-1 at --std 85 (COBOL0871), since the 1985 format prints only identifier-1. The witness rewrites from a shorter and a longer alphanumeric item and a group, and shows the move done even when the REWRITE then fails with status 23. Probed further at --std 85: a numeric sender to a numeric record aligns on the decimal point (12.34 to 9(8)V9(4) stores 000000123400), a COMP sender converts, a subscripted sender and a JUSTIFIED RIGHT record follow MOVE, an alphanumeric-edited sender to a numeric record draws COBOL0819 and an index data item COBOL0809. A sender in the record's own storage draws nothing; that is the syntax rule §1985:IX.4.6.3 SR1, kb/Work PB5077, not this rule.

next.reason: 2023 adds FROM literal-1 (§2023:14.9.35.4 GR7: "MOVE literal-1 TO record-name-1"), which the 1985 format refuses; the FROM identifier-1 case is unchanged. 1985: REWRITE FROM equals 'MOVE identifier-1 TO record-name-1' per the MOVE rules, then the REWRITE without FROM. §2023:14.9.35.4 GR7 states the same equivalence, and §2023:14.9.35.3 SR6 states the MOVE-validity part as a syntax rule. FROM literal-1 is new syntax; a 1985 program means the same.
